help.title: About Commissions
help.overview: A Commission is the agent payout row created from a reservation or a sale. This is the ledger, not the Agent report (which is a period performance view). Status moves pending → pending approval → paid, or voided when the source deal is cancelled or a payment is reversed.

sections.title: What a commission holds
items: Source type: reservation or sale, plus the source record.
Agent, amounts, currency, rates that were used when it was recorded.
Status: pending, pending approval, paid, voided.
Evidence / notes depending on how your roles expose the fields.

sections.title: How it is created
items: Paying or reinstating a reservation records a reservation commission.
A sale records a sale commission according to the sale/reservation rates (project or unit override).
You should not invent a commission with no source deal — it would not stay consistent with Dashboard or Agent report.

sections.title: How it behaves
items: Cancelling a reservation or reversing an unpaid reservation deposit voids pending commission — not one already marked paid.
Reversing a reservation payment is blocked if this commission is already paid.
Paying a commission here is the payout step. Agent report still only reads deals in a date range; it does not mark paid.

sections.title: Related records
items: Reservation or Sale, agent user, Unit. Agent report. ERP export can include a commissions dataset.
